content:
I am preparing materials for a research project on how people categorize everyday social
and economic situations. Three existing vignettes need revision. Keep each protagonist's
name, the character type (firm/business), and the setting type; change only what the
revision goal asks.

CURRENT VIGNETTES

B4 (class: indignant responder; firm; entrusted proceeds): Silas stocks his delicatessen with estate olive oil fronted by importer Corbin, selling at Corbin's set price and remitting proceeds minus a fifth. Midway through the season, Silas finds Corbin's own website offering identical bottles at nearly half that price: his shop existed as the overpriced front that made Corbin's 'direct discount' look like a bargain. Silas crates every remaining bottle back to the warehouse, refunds his buyers from the till, and closes the account, forfeiting his fifth.

S3 (class: own-payoff responder; firm; responding to proposed terms): Aiko owns a print shop. A hotel chain proposes a year-long contract: rock-bottom rates, strict deadlines, and a clause letting the chain cancel monthly while Aiko cannot. She works the numbers once — the volume covers her presses' idle hours and clears a profit, thin but positive. That settles it. Whether the chain gains vastly more from the arrangement is not a column in her spreadsheet.

S4 (class: own-payoff responder; firm; entrusted proceeds): Lorcan runs an auction house. An estate executor delivered furniture to sell, with a handshake understanding about remitting proceeds after a standard commission. The paperwork, though, lets Lorcan add handling, storage, and listing fees at his discretion. He layers on every fee the contract permits and remits the minimum the documents require, having checked only which charges no court could claw back.

REVISION GOALS

B4: The responder discovers the same mistreatment by the counterpart, and responds by
KEEPING the proceeds in his own hands as compensation for how he was used---punitive
toward the counterpart and materially self-serving at the same time, rather than
refunding third parties or giving everything up. The condemnation of the counterpart's
conduct must remain the clear driver; the responder may accept some risk or cost of
conflict, but he ends up keeping what he holds.

S3 and S4: Remove any hint of sharp practice, exploitation, or gaming of contracts.
The responder should come across as a neutral, unsentimental payoff calculator acting
within ordinary business terms: they take the deal or keep the share that leaves their
own firm best off, and the other side's outcome simply does not enter the decision.
No fee-stacking, no legal-loophole reasoning, no wording that invites a judgment of
misconduct.

CONSTRAINTS (unchanged from the original generation)

1. 50-80 words, third person, one named responder and one clearly identified other party.
2. Do NOT use the words "fair", "unfair", "selfish", "generous", "greedy", "cooperate",
   "cooperation", "moral", "trust", "betray", or their derivatives.
3. Do not mention experiments, studies, games, players, laboratories, or questionnaires.
4. Do not use the dollar amounts 6, 12, or 18, and do not use a tripling of any amount.
5. Keep the protagonist names (Silas, Aiko, Lorcan) and counterpart identities.

OUTPUT FORMAT

Return a single JSON object, no other text:
{"replacements": [{"id": "B4", "text": "..."}, {"id": "S3", "text": "..."},
{"id": "S4", "text": "..."}]}

{"replacements": [{"id": "B4", "text": "Silas stocks his delicatessen with estate olive oil fronted by importer Corbin, selling at Corbin's set price and remitting proceeds minus a fifth. Midway through the season, Silas finds Corbin's website selling identical bottles at nearly half that price: his shop was the overpriced front making Corbin's 'direct discount' look like a bargain. Incensed at being used as a prop, Silas keeps the season's proceeds as payment for the charade and tells Corbin to sue if he likes."}, {"id": "S3", "text": "Aiko owns a print shop. A hotel chain proposes a year-long printing contract at rates below her usual list: menus, signage, stationery on a fixed monthly schedule. She runs the numbers once — the guaranteed volume fills her presses' idle hours and yields a modest but reliable margin. That settles it; she signs. Whether the chain's savings dwarf her profit is not a column in her spreadsheet."}, {"id": "S4", "text": "Lorcan runs an auction house. An estate executor consigned furniture under a written agreement: sale at auction, a standard commission to Lorcan, the balance remitted within thirty days. The pieces sell well. Lorcan deducts his full contracted commission — the same rate he charges every consignor — and wires the remainder on schedule. Whether the executor considers the proceeds ample or thin plays no part in his accounting; his rate covers costs and margin."}]}
